verdict_text:
YES

The script drops exactly the 48 buffers, casts exactly the 64 projection matrices to bfloat16 via `.float().to(torch.bfloat16)` (equivalent to a direct cast per clause 1), upcasts everything else to float32, preserves names, and asserts all four required checks before writing. Anchored `fullmatch` on both regexes prevents the over-broad-targeting hazard. The only part I cannot verify by reading is the sharding/index behaviour, which is delegated to `save_sharded_safetensors` in the unshown `_ckpt` module; the 256 MiB limit is passed correctly, so correctness of clause 5 rests on that helper.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
